Package org.cyborgcats.ssm

Class Scheduler

java.lang.Object
org.cyborgcats.ssm.Scheduler
public class Scheduler extends Object
Singleton scheduler for the state-machine system (SSM) that manages the lifecycle of active State objects and drives the button-polling loop each robot cycle.

    • schedule

      public final void schedule(State newState)
      Schedules a new state for execution. If the state conflicts with a currently active state whose requirements overlap and that state is not interruptible, the new state is silently dropped. Otherwise, conflicting states have their State.onInterrupt(Runnable) callback invoked and their cleanup states (if any) scheduled. State.onEnd(Runnable) is not invoked on this path.

      While the robot is disabled, only states exempted via State.withIgnoreDisable(boolean) are accepted; anything else is silently dropped before any conflict is resolved, so a rejected state never interrupts a running one.

      Parameters:
      newState - the state to schedule; a null value is silently ignored

    • end

      public final void end(State state)
      Forcibly ends the given state and schedules its cleanup state (if any). Has no effect if the state is not currently active.

      Neither the state's State.onEnd(Runnable) nor its State.onInterrupt(Runnable) callback is invoked; attach teardown logic to the cleanup state instead.

      The cleanup state is scheduled through schedule(State), so while the robot is disabled it runs only if it is itself exempt via State.withIgnoreDisable(boolean).

      Parameters:
      state - the state to end

    • run

      public final void run()
      Advances all active states by one loop iteration, removes finished states (invoking their State.onEnd(Runnable) callback and scheduling their finish states if defined), and then runs every registered button-polling callback. Should be called once per robot loop from robotPeriodic.

      While the robot is disabled, every active state that is not exempt is ended as if interrupted: its State.onInterrupt(Runnable) callback runs and its cleanup state is offered to schedule(State), which accepts the cleanup only if that cleanup is itself exempt. Teardown that must survive a disable therefore has to be marked exempt as well.

      The button loop still polls while disabled, so triggers keep their edge state in sync and a condition held across the disable boundary does not fire a spurious edge on re-enable.

      A step body may safely call schedule(State) or end(State) while this method is running; a state scheduled that way first runs on the following loop.
